name: Shelemiah
title: Descendant of Levi
summary: Shelemiah was a Levite mentioned in the book of Ezra in connection with the return from exile in Babylon. He was among those found to have married a foreign wife and committed to sending her away in accordance with Ezra's reforms to preserve the people's purity and faithfulness to God's covenant.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among Those With Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: Shelemiah is mentioned among the Levites who had taken foreign wives during the aftermath of the exile, which was contrary to God's covenant law.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's Reform Movement
keyEvents.description: Ezra led a major reform movement in which the people confessed their sin of marrying women from foreign nations, and Shelemiah was among those affected.

keyEvents.title: The Assembly in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: All the people were summoned to Jerusalem to take a stand on the issue of foreign wives, and it was decided that they should separate themselves from them.

keyEvents.title: Examination of the Marriages
keyEvents.description: A commission was appointed to investigate all cases of marriage with foreign women, and Shelemiah was among those examined and found guilty.
